findings.title: feature request: a state change reason for clawbacks, which are stored as BURN like a payment to the issuer
findings.cause: The state change vocabulary has no CLAWBACK reason. Clawback and ClawbackClaimableBalance write a BALANCE BURN row (and a DEBIT), so the CAP-67 `clawback` event of the ledger is stored as a `burn`. wallet-backend documents this as intended (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L92), so the draft is a feature request.

findings.title: transaction participants from meta are never collected (participantsForMeta reads the TransactionMeta V0 arm)
findings.cause: participantsForMeta switches on `meta.Operations`, the V0 arm of the TransactionMeta union, which is nil for v1 to v4 meta, so accounts that only the meta shows (the sponsor of a claimed or clawed-back claimable balance) are never participants, while accounts only the envelope names (claimants, a payment destination that is the issuer) are. The extra envelope-named participants match wallet-backend's documented rule (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L119-L124); the dropped meta-only ones are the bug. Already reported upstream as #677 (open); the draft is a comment for it with a concrete dropped sponsor.

findings.title: question: BALANCE rows for claimable balance and liquidity pool transfers do not record the balance or pool
findings.cause: BALANCE rows are written per account; the claimable balance (B) or liquidity pool (L) end of a transfer has no row, so the stored transfer has a null counterparty and the ledger's transfer event to or from the B or L address has no counterpart. The single row is documented (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L67-L68, from #442), so the draft asks whether the B or L address belongs in it.

findings.title: a text, hash or return memo of a payment to a G address is stored nowhere
findings.cause: CAP-67 puts the transaction memo of a payment to a G address into the transfer event's `to_muxed_id` as u64, string or bytes; wallet-backend stores `to_muxed_id` only for u64 values and no table has a memo column, so text, hash and return memos are stored nowhere.

findings.title: contract deployments that no auth entry declares (factory deploys, Stellar Asset Contracts) record no contract creation
findings.cause: Contract creation rows come only from the operation's own CreateContract with a FromAddress preimage and from CreateContract invocations declared in auth entries, so a contract deployed by another contract without an auth entry, and any Stellar Asset Contract deployment, gets no ACCOUNT CREATE row although the meta creates the instance.

findings.title: an XLM transfer through the native asset contract that creates the destination account records no account creation
findings.cause: From protocol 26 (CAP-73) an XLM SAC transfer to a missing G account creates it; wallet-backend writes ACCOUNT CREATE only for CreateAccount operations, so the new account gets a credit but no creation row.

findings.title: a pool-share trustline removed by an authorization revocation records no trustline removal
findings.cause: Revoking authorization with SetTrustLineFlags or AllowTrust redeems the holder's pool shares and removes the pool-share trustline (CAP-38). The removal is in the meta; wallet-backend writes no TRUSTLINE REMOVE for it.

findings.title: a pre-auth signer core removes in txChangesBefore is never recorded as removed (failed transactions, fee bumps)
findings.cause: Core removes a transaction's pre-auth signer in txChangesBefore whether the transaction succeeds or fails, and a fee bump's from the fee source before the inner transaction; wallet-backend derives SIGNER rows only from operation effects of successful transactions, so neither removal is stored.

findings.title: question: CreateAccount writes a SIGNER ADD row for the new account's master key (Horizon parity); intended for state changes?
findings.cause: Following Horizon's effects (the code says it was ported from them), account creation emits a signer-created state change for the master key, and set options treats the master key as a signer while its weight is above 0. The ledger has no signer entry: the master key's weight is byte 0 of the account's thresholds. Likely intended; the draft asks, and what it would cost consumers is that the row looks like a signer entry.

findings.title: ContractDeployProcessor walks the declared auth invocation tree with no depth limit (indexerlint IDX002)
findings.reproduce: indexerlint -format json ./... (in a checkout of wallet-backend at 3e22515a44979fdc3a558fda3991ca2b48e38cef)
findings.cause: The walkInvocation closure in (*ContractDeployProcessor).ProcessOperation recurses over xdr.SorobanAuthorizedInvocation with no depth counter. The walk runs only for successful transactions, and the decoder (depth 1500) and core (envelopes nested deeper than 1000 XDR levels are refused from protocol 28) bound it today, so it is a hardening finding, not a halt.

findings.title: xdr.DecodeOptions.MaxDepth counts fewer levels per nesting than stellar-xdr, so the sdk decodes envelopes nested deeper than core accepts
findings.cause: go-xdr spends one depth unit per named type, while stellar-xdr, which core runs at depth 1000 from protocol 28, also counts each optional and each array. On v0.9.0 the deepest auth chain decoded is 988 at MaxDepth 1000 (1488 at the default 1500) against core's 493, and the deepest nested ScVec argument 495 (745) against 246, so the sdk accepts auth trees and ScVals that core refuses.

findings.title: strkey decoders before v0.9.0 accept strkeys with carriage returns, newlines or 0xff bytes added
findings.cause: Decode, DecodeAny and Version checked the canonical length on the raw input, then go's encoding/base32 skipped carriage returns and newlines and read 0xff as padding, so such a string decoded to the payload of the strkey it was added to. Fixed in v0.9.0 by #6026, which rejects any byte outside the base32 alphabet first.

findings.title: fromXdr decodes envelopes nested deeper than stellar-core accepts, and no maxDepth value matches core's limit
findings.cause: Core refuses envelopes nested deeper than its decode limit; the sdk's default (1500 nested schemas since js-xdr#155) is wider and cannot be lowered through fromXdr, and through schema.decode core's boundary falls at a different maxDepth per shape, so no single value matches core.

findings.title: question: the XDR-JSON reader accepts 64-bit integer strings with a plus sign, "-0" or leading zeros
findings.cause: NumberOrString passes a JSON string to str::parse, so "+16", "-0" and "016" read as 16 and 0; the crate's own tests assert this, so the draft is a question. The failing checks are "+16" and "-0" in the non-canonical entry; negative ids such as "-16" are valid int64 values that core refuses only in doCheckValid, so they are in the negative entry, which accepts the exact id the crate reads.

findings.title: the XDR-JSON reader stops at serde_json's recursion limit of 128, so values the crate writes as JSON cannot be read back
findings.cause: to_xdr_json renders nested values of any depth the decoder accepts, but the reader uses serde_json with its default recursion limit, so deep auth trees, ScVals and events (including ones on recorded protocol 30 ledgers) do not round-trip through JSON.

findings.title: bool decodes any u32 and reads everything but 1 as false, where core reads non-zero as true and go-stellar-sdk refuses
findings.cause: impl ReadXdr for bool returns i == 1 for any u32, so the word 2 decodes as false and re-encodes as 0, where go-stellar-sdk and js-stellar-sdk refuse it and core's xdrpp reads it as true. The differential fuzzer found the same class through every fuzzed type that carries a bool (findings/fuzz/known-classes.txt).

findings.title: core (xdrpp) accepts a bool word other than 0 or 1 as true and hashes its own re-encoding with 1
findings.cause: xdrpp's xdr_traits<bool>::from_uint is u != 0, and the enum check runs on the converted value, so core decodes any non-zero bool word as true. The transaction hash, the signature check and the protocol 28 rust parse check all use core's re-encoding (word 1), never the submitted bytes. In a local core 30.0.0 run an envelope with the word 2 signed over the canonical hash was applied with txSUCCESS and stored with 1; signed over the submitted bytes it got txBAD_AUTH. Low severity: no authorization bypass or fund loss, but the hash of the submitted bytes differs from core's transaction hash and stellar-xdr reads the same argument as false. The matched cells are the rust testee diverging from its peers on the envelope form (the fuzz classes in findings/fuzz/known-classes.txt are the same root cause).
